page: Microsoft Azure E20d_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance delivers 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1 data cache per core. Compute instruction extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES hardware cryptography.

The configuration provides 160.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is bundled via an integrated 805 GB SSD, offering high-speed scratch space directly on the host node. The server does not include dedicated graphics processing units, relying entirely on CPU-based compute operations.

Benchmark results place the memory subsystem in the upper tier, with the PassMark memory evaluation achieving strong results (2,791.74) and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 90.14 GB/sec. General multi-core processing demonstrates average performance across synthetic tests, producing 18,627.31 in stress-ng multi-core and 8,491.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-core stress testing registers lower throughput at 1,411.88, reflecting the modest 2.6 GHz base clock speed. In-memory data structures perform solidly, registering 17.19 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 7,212.1 in PassMark database operations.

This hardware balance yields qualitative resource density for memory-bound applications without forcing the user to provision unneeded compute cores. The integrated 805 GB local SSD avoids standard network-storage latencies for temporary caching, indexing, and buffer operations. Microsoft Azure E20d_v4 is well suited for production relational database servers, enterprise in-memory caches, big data analytics engines, and large-scale ETL pipelines that require generous RAM allocation alongside moderate compute capacity.
